raw_response:
I am 73, been farming these 5.5 mu for 50 years. Only went to primary school, so I know my letters and numbers but most of what I know comes from working the land and watching neighbors. My wife and I, just the two of us now — children went to the city long ago.

This year I plant stevia on most of my land. Stevia pays better than cotton now, the buyers come from the company and they want the leaves. I keep a small piece of cotton because I always have, and cotton is what I know best. Maybe 1 mu cotton, 4.5 mu stevia.

For stevia, I buy the seedlings from the same dealer as last year — he gives me the improved kind, everybody around here uses them. I put down chicken manure in winter, 2 cart loads per mu if I can get it, then before transplanting I spread compound fertilizer 15-15-15, about 2 bags (100 jin, 50 kg) per mu. After the plants take root I top-dress with urea, maybe 20 jin (10 kg) per mu, and again after first cutting another 20 jin. Stevia needs water — I irrigate from the well maybe 6-7 times through the season, after transplanting, after each cutting, and when the leaves look tired in the hot days. I spray for aphids and leaf-eating worms maybe 3-4 times. Last year I got about 300 kg dried leaves per mu, I aim for the same.

For cotton, I stick to what works. Improved seed from the supply station. I put diammonium phosphate before planting, 1 bag (50 jin, 25 kg) per mu, and urea top-dress 30 jin (15 kg) when it flowers, plus another 20 jin at boll. Cotton wants water 4 times from my well. Bollworm and aphid spray — at least 5 times, cotton bugs are bad. I plough the cotton ground, stevia I just rotary-till because the roots stay. I expect about 250 kg seed cotton per mu, same as last year.

I don't like to change much. What I did last year gave me enough, so I do the same.
